# `Q-2-10` — Closing Quote Without Matching Open Quote

> A closing single-quote mark appears with no opening
> single-quote earlier in the block.

## What this means

Quarto markdown treats single quotes as a paired construct. A `'`
that is not directly attached to a word is read as a quote mark:
when it opens a quote that the parser then cannot close, because a
space follows it, it raises this error.

The diagnostic message points at the quote mark as the trigger; the
actual mistake is usually a stray `'` or a missing opening quote.

## Why this happens

A `'` directly after a word is an apostrophe, and never produces
this error: `it's`, `don't`, `Mary's`, the plural possessives `the
dogs' toys` and `the cats'.`, and `d'` before a code span all render
as written, with a typographic apostrophe.

The error fires for a `'` followed by a space that the parser
cannot attach to a word:
one with whitespace in front of it (`the admins ' console`), one
after a closing delimiter such as `` ` `` or `**`, and one after a
word that starts with a digit or a non-ASCII letter (`the 1990s'
music`, `Agnès' house`).

## How to fix

If the mark is a stray character, remove it or close the space before
it. If the construction really is a quotation, add the opening `'` at
the intended start.

For a literal apostrophe that the parser keeps mis-reading, escape
it:

```markdown
The 1990s\' music; `a.rs`\'s module.
```

## Example

```markdown
a ' b.
```

The `'` after `a ` is read as a quote that opens and is never
closed.
